title: Fundamentals of Quantum Entanglement
text:
Quantum entanglement is a physical phenomenon occurring when two or more particles become linked in such a way that they share the same quantum state. Measuring a property (such as spin) on one entangled particle instantly influences the corresponding property of the other, regardless of the spatial distance separating them.

The correlation between these measurements is stronger than any classical statistical correlation can account for, famously leading Einstein to dub it 'spooky action at a distance.' This non-local connection has profound implications for how physics understands reality and information transfer. While entanglement does not permit faster-than-light communication of classical data, it is the central resource fueling emerging quantum technologies.

The study of entanglement is crucial in developing powerful computational tools, particularly quantum computing, where linked particle states are utilized to perform calculations impossible for classical machines.
